high.title: Peso May Stay Weak on Revived Conflict
high.summary: The PHP closed at P61.587/USD on Friday, recovering a marginal 3.3 centavos from Thursday's P61.62, but still registering a net weekly loss of 7.2 centavos versus the P61.515 close on July 10. The primary driver of peso weakness is the re-escalation of the Middle East conflict, which is fueling broad risk-off sentiment and supporting USD safe-haven demand. Markets are described as largely directionless, trading in a tight P61.555–P61.62 range amid a lack of fresh domestic catalysts. For FX traders, the near-term bias remains tilted to the downside for the peso, with geopolitical developments in the Middle East serving as the key swing factor. Should tensions intensify further, a test of the P62.00 level cannot be ruled out. Watch for any BSP intervention signals if depreciation accelerates, as well as upcoming US economic data releases that could shift Fed rate expectations and add another layer of volatility to the USD/PHP pair.

high.title: Yields Mixed on Iran Conflict, Soft US Data
high.summary: Philippine government securities yields moved mixed last week but broadly rose by an average of 7.4 basis points week-on-week at the secondary market, based on PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service (BVAL) Reference Rates as of July 17. The dual drivers were renewed Middle East tensions — which triggered a risk-off flight and pushed yields higher — and softer-than-expected US inflation data, which prompted traders to reprice Federal Reserve rate cut expectations, creating cross-currents across the yield curve. For Philippine bond investors, this is a critical dynamic: geopolitical risk is pressuring yields upward (prices lower), while a more dovish Fed repricing could provide a partial offset by anchoring the long end. The net 7.4 bps average rise signals caution in the market. Investors should closely monitor the trajectory of US CPI data and Middle East developments, as both will continue to drive sentiment in Philippine government bonds in the near term. A sustained rise in GS yields would also increase the government's borrowing costs.

high.title: Government Debt Rates May Be Mixed as Treasury Increases Offer Volumes
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) is resuming its Cash Management Bill (CMB) issuance program this week, offering up to P90 billion in combined short-term securities on Monday — comprising P40 billion in CMBs (split between 35-day and 63-day tenors) alongside its regular T-bill offerings. The increased supply injection comes at a challenging moment, with market sentiment already under pressure from the re-escalation of the Middle East conflict. Analysts expect debt rates to end mixed, as the supply surge could push short-end yields higher, while broader risk-off dynamics and any Fed dovish repricing may cap the upside at the longer end. For bond traders and fund managers, the key question is whether demand will be sufficient to absorb the heavier issuance without a significant yield spike. The bid-to-cover ratios at these auctions will serve as an important real-time gauge of investor appetite for Philippine sovereign paper amid current volatility. Watch auction results closely as a signal for near-term GS market direction.

high.title: Peso Falls as US-Iran Clashes Push Up Oil
high.summary:
The Philippine Peso depreciated 9.9 centavos to close at P61.686/USD on Monday, snapping a three-session winning streak. The selloff was driven by escalating US-Iran military clashes in the Middle East, which pushed global crude oil prices sharply higher and reignited inflation concerns for the Philippines — a net oil importer. The peso opened the session already on the back foot at P61.65, which proved to be its intraday high, indicating sustained selling pressure throughout the day.

**Why it matters:** Rising oil prices represent a dual threat for the peso — they widen the trade deficit by inflating the import bill, and they stoke domestic inflation, potentially complicating the BSP's monetary easing path. For FX traders, the P61.70 level should be watched as near-term resistance. A sustained breach toward P62.00 is plausible if the Middle East conflict intensifies further. Bond investors should also monitor whether oil-driven inflation expectations begin repricing the short end of the yield curve, which could delay anticipated BSP rate cuts.

high.title: Yields on Short-Term Bills Move Sideways as War Stokes Volatility
high.summary:
The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) made a full P80 billion award of its combined Cash Management Bills (CMBs) and Treasury bills (T-bills) on Monday, drawing strong demand as total tenders reached P210.025 billion — representing an oversubscription ratio of approximately 2.6x. Yields were mixed, moving broadly sideways against the backdrop of heightened global volatility stemming from fresh Middle East hostilities. The reissuance of CMBs after a two-week hiatus signals the government's continued appetite for short-duration cash management financing.

**Why it matters:** The robust bid-to-cover ratio of ~2.6x confirms solid investor appetite for Philippine short-term paper despite external headwinds, suggesting the domestic liquidity environment remains ample. However, the sideways yield movement — rather than a decisive rally — indicates that markets are cautious, with geopolitical risk and potential oil-driven inflation offsetting any bullish momentum. Bond investors should watch whether Middle East developments cause yields to drift higher in the coming sessions, particularly on the 91-day and 182-day tenors, which are most sensitive to near-term BSP policy rate expectations.

high.title: Philippines' FDI Outlook Remains Weak for Rest of 2026
high.summary:
The Philippines is expected to face continued headwinds in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) through the remainder of 2026, driven by persistent geopolitical risks and domestic governance concerns, according to economists. UA&P economist Marco Antonio Agonia flagged that the domestic economy remains vulnerable to external shocks, suggesting subdued FDI growth is likely for the near term. For FX traders, weak FDI inflows are a structural negative for the PHP, as they reduce a key source of USD supply into the domestic economy, potentially adding depreciation pressure on the peso. For bond investors, prolonged FDI weakness could dampen economic growth prospects and complicate the fiscal outlook, which may weigh on sentiment for Philippine government securities. Equity investors in the PSEi should also take note, as foreign portfolio flows often correlate with FDI sentiment. Key factors to monitor include any policy announcements aimed at improving the investment climate, geopolitical developments affecting regional risk appetite, and BSP's response to sustained external account pressures.

---

medium.title: BSP Securities' Rate Inches Higher
medium.summary:
The BSP's 28-day securities auction saw rates edge marginally higher, with the central bank fully awarding its P40 billion offering. Total tenders reached P70.69 billion, reflecting a bid-to-cover ratio of 1.7673x — still comfortably oversubscribed but down from the prior week's 2.006x ratio on P80.24 billion in bids. The slight softening in demand and the incremental rise in the accepted rate are worth monitoring, as BSP bill auctions serve as a proxy for short-term liquidity conditions and market expectations around the BSP's policy stance. A continued drift higher in BSP bill rates could signal the beginning of a tightening of short-end financial conditions, with implications for both the PHP and the front end of the GS yield curve.

---

medium.title: Banks' Cash Withdrawals from BSP Post Slower Growth on Weak Demand
medium.summary:
BSP data from its 2025 Annual Report reveals that banknote withdrawals by banks grew at a significantly slower pace of 6.2% to P1.568 trillion in 2025, down sharply from 12.5% growth recorded in 2024, reflecting tighter economic conditions and weaker cash demand. This deceleration in physical currency circulation is consistent with a broader slowdown in economic activity and/or a continued structural shift toward digital payments. For monetary policy watchers, softer cash demand may reinforce the BSP's view that domestic liquidity conditions are not excessively loose, potentially supporting the case for further rate cuts. While not a primary FX or bond market driver, the data provides a useful supplementary read on the health of domestic credit and economic momentum — both relevant inputs for peso and PSEi positioning.

---

medium.title: Fuel Retailers Urged to Stagger Double-Digit Price Hikes
medium.summary: Diesel and kerosene pump prices are set to surge by more than P10 per liter starting July 21, with gasoline rising by up to P3.65 per liter, prompting the Department of Energy to appeal to oil companies to stagger the increases and offer discounts to public utilities. These sharp fuel price hikes carry meaningful inflation implications, as energy costs feed directly into transport and food supply chain costs — two major components of the Philippine CPI basket. For BSP watchers, a significant inflation uptick stemming from fuel prices could complicate the Monetary Board's rate-cutting calculus, potentially delaying further easing and supporting short-end PHP rates. FX traders should monitor whether sustained inflationary pressure shifts BSP's forward guidance, as a more hawkish tilt would be broadly supportive of the peso.

medium.title: Pay Raises in Philippines Seen Edging Up in 2027 — WTW
medium.summary: Philippine companies plan to raise salaries by a median of 5.1% in 2027, marginally above the 5.0% average increase in 2026, according to a WTW survey, as firms balance rising business costs with talent retention needs. While a modest uptick, wage growth at this level adds a secondary inflationary impulse to the demand side of the economy, which is relevant for BSP's medium-term inflation forecasting. Combined with the fuel price surge reported separately today, building cost-push and wage-driven inflation pressures could keep BSP cautious on the pace of monetary easing — a factor worth monitoring for both PHP and Philippine government bond positioning.

medium.title: Stocks Stay Above 6,400 on Earnings Optimism
medium.summary: The PSEi extended its winning streak to four consecutive sessions, gaining 0.18% (+11.61 points) to close at 6,415.72, with the broader All Shares index also rising 0.19% to 3,450.69. The advance was driven by optimism around Q2 corporate earnings and continued bargain hunting. However, renewed geopolitical risks — particularly fresh tensions pushing global oil prices higher — remain a headwind worth monitoring. For equity investors, the sustained hold above the 6,400 level is technically constructive, though upside may be capped if oil-driven inflationary pressures re-emerge and weigh on BSP rate-cut expectations. Rising oil prices could also exert mild depreciation pressure on the PHP given the Philippines' import-dependent energy profile.

medium.title: Rally May Lose Steam as Market Seeks Fresh Leads
medium.summary: The PSEi posted its best close in over four months on Friday, surging 1.24% (+78.96 points) to 6,404.11, with the All Shares index rising 0.88% to 3,444.07. Analysts caution, however, that momentum may be difficult to sustain this week given an absence of strong domestic catalysts and renewed Middle East hostilities reigniting market volatility. For fund managers, the key risk is whether geopolitical-driven oil price spikes translate into broader risk-off sentiment, which could trigger foreign equity outflows and renewed PHP selling pressure. The market will likely look to upcoming earnings releases and any BSP policy signals for directional cues.
